topics.topic: Caller and authorization boundary for recognition-publication decoding
questions: Is this operation called directly by the external OCR-service boundary, or by `module:api` while handling the authenticated staff submission required by R0-17 and the State 4 flow?

Because the State 4 flow says the API route calls this operation, the passage must name `module:api` as a caller and the authoritative `module_internal` surface must include `expense_intake.decode_recognition_publication`; otherwise the route-call text must be removed.

Who actually calls this operation and at what boundary: the unauthenticated OCR service, `module:api` after staff authorization, or neither because the route has already decoded the body into the same model?

Who actually calls `decode_recognition_publication`, and at what point relative to staff authentication and project authorization? The received product text says the OCR service has no portal principal and authenticated staff submits the recognition, while the flow says the route calls this operation after its guard.

quotes:
`boundary:ocr_service`: the confirmed recognition the external OCR service
publishes, before it reaches the consumer. The HTTP route decodes its request
body with its own model check; the consumer checks the version again.

1. The route authorizes with
   `capability:authorization_guard.authorize_staff_project_mutation`.
   A recognition payload that arrives undecoded from the OCR service is
   decoded at expense_intake's public boundary,
   `capability:expense_intake.decode_recognition_publication`, which refuses
   a malformed payload or a `contract_version` outside
   `SUPPORTED_OCR_CONTRACT_VERSIONS` with `ExpenseValidationError` before
   the payload reaches `create_expense_from_recognition`; decoding reads and
   writes nothing (A7; owner 2026-11-08, Q09). The route's own request
   decoding keeps its model check; the consumer below checks the version
   again.
judgement.divergence: The OCR-service boundary calls the decoder directly without staff authorization, or module:api calls it only after the staff project-mutation guard; the OCR integration and HTTP caller observe different callable boundaries and failure precedence.
judgement.why: State 5 names the external OCR boundary as the caller, while the earlier flow requires the authenticated route to authorize and then invoke the decoder.

An expense is created when an authenticated staff member with mutation
capability on the project submits the confirmed recognition result with the
project and the allocation; a progress photo is published the same way. The
intake interface and OCR decide nothing. The portal trusts that authenticated
staff submission and records its `provenance_ref`; it does not verify
independently that the content came from the OCR service, which has no
principal of its own in the portal.

topics.topic: Exact JSON validation, coercion, and unknown-field policy for recognition publications
questions: Must decoding reject JSON objects containing every required field plus unknown fields, or may it ignore/preserve unknown fields?
What exact JSON representations and coercions are accepted for `Decimal`, UUID, date, datetime, enum and integer fields when producing `ConfirmedRecognitionPublication`?
What exact JSON-decoding policy defines “complete,” including unknown/provider/raw fields, coercion of strings to decimals or dates, duplicate line IDs, and invalid normalized-item values?
What exact JSON encodings, coercions and unknown-field policy define a valid `ConfirmedRecognitionPublication`, especially for `Decimal`, `date`, `datetime`, enum and nested item fields?

quotes: The undecoded payload, a JSON object.

`ExpenseValidationError` for a payload that is not a complete
`ConfirmedRecognitionPublication` and for a `contract_version` outside
`SUPPORTED_OCR_CONTRACT_VERSIONS`. It carries no payload content.

questions: Does this operation request `projects`, `projects/active`, or `REGISTRY_PROJECTS_PATH` joined with `REGISTRY_ACTIVE_SEGMENT`, and must it still filter decoded entries by status?
Does the operation request `REGISTRY_PROJECTS_PATH` alone, or join it with `REGISTRY_ACTIVE_SEGMENT` as A6 and A30 require for `projects/active`?

Does the operation request `projects/active`, request plain `projects`, or treat `REGISTRY_PROJECTS_PATH` itself as the complete `projects/active` path? This conflicts with the received Registry v1 contract requiring `REGISTRY_PROJECTS_PATH` and `REGISTRY_ACTIVE_SEGMENT` to be joined.

topics.topic: Whether re-allocation also updates the parent Expense audit fields
questions: Does an accepted re-allocation also replace the `Expense` with new `updated_at` and `updated_by`, as A19 now requires, or does it change only allocation rows as this State impact says?

quotes: Replaces the expense's allocations; appends one `AuditRecord`.

Owner 2026-11-08: every accepted include or exclude of an expense — also one
that leaves `included` as it was — replaces the Expense with `included`,
`updated_at` (the operation's one instant) and `updated_by` (the acting
staff member) (Q01); every accepted metadata update of an expense document
sets the document's `updated_by` to the acting staff member as well as its
`updated_at` (Q02); a re-allocation is a change of the Expense: it replaces
the Expense with new `updated_at` and `updated_by`, and the returned
aggregate holds that replaced Expense with the new allocations (Q03). Q01
and Q03 confirm the running service; Q02 likewise. No amount, provenance or
allocation rule changes.
judgement.divergence: One implementation replaces only allocation rows and leaves Expense.updated_at/updated_by unchanged; the other also replaces the parent Expense with the operation instant and actor and returns it in the aggregate; the API caller and later repository readers observe the metadata difference.
judgement.why: The State 5 impact lists only allocation replacement, while A19 explicitly requires every accepted re-allocation to replace the parent Expense and update its change metadata.
